newsitem.title: GERMANY: SOCCER-STUTTGART IN HIGH-SCORING ROMP OVER COLOGNE.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-STUTTGART IN HIGH-SCORING ROMP OVER COLOGNE.

text.p: High-scoring Stuttgart trounced Cologne 4-0 on Sunday to remain unbeaten and hot on the heels of Bundesliga leaders Bayern Munich.
With an unblemished record of four straight wins, Stuttgart have 12 points from their four matches and trail Bayern Munich, who have won four and tied one in their five games, by just one point.
Stuttgart, who lead the league in scoring with 14 goals in their four matches, erupted after a scoreless first half.
Defender Thomas Schneider headed home from a corner in the 49th minute and Croatian Zvonimir Soldo added the second two minutes later.
Giovane Elber scored off a brilliant pass from German national Freddie Bobic in the 72nd minute and Krassimir Balakow made it 4-0 in the 78th minute.
"The two goals right after half-time brought us down the right path," said Stuttgart trainer Joachim Loew. "It is tremendous that we have once again not allowed a goal."
Stuttgart have allowed just one goal in four games this year to led the league in defence as well as offence.
On Saturday, Bayern Munich defeated Arminia Bielefeld 1-0 and defending champion Borussia Dortmund, currently tied for second with Stuttgart, stopped Rostock 1-0 with a 90th minute goal.
